_readme: Two extra tools for the 'MCP Server - n8n Self API' workflow, so the connector can
create credentials as well as workflows.
To add them: open that workflow in n8n, click on empty canvas, and paste this whole
file (Ctrl+V). n8n turns pasted JSON into real nodes. Then drag a connection from each
new node's top connector up to the MCP Server Trigger's 'Tool' input.
Pasting is non-destructive - unlike update_workflow, which replaces the whole workflow.
Note: n8n's API can CREATE credentials but never read them back. There is no
list-credentials endpoint, by design - secrets do not come back out. So create_credential
returns an id and that is the only handle you get.

parameters.toolDescription: Create a new credential on this n8n instance. The body must be a JSON object with the keys name, type and data. Example: {"name":"Academia Webhook Auth","type":"httpHeaderAuth","data":{"name":"Authorization","value":"Bearer SECRET"}}. Returns the new credential id. Call get_credential_schema first if unsure which fields a type needs. Credentials cannot be listed or read back afterwards - n8n never returns secret values.
parameters.jsonBody: ={{ $fromAI('credentialJson', 'Credential as a JSON string with exactly the keys name, type and data', 'string') }}

parameters.toolDescription: Fetch the required data fields for one n8n credential type, for example httpHeaderAuth or openRouterApi. Use this before create_credential so the data object uses the right field names.
